findings.text: follow-on: _CREDENTIAL_STATUS_PATTERN = re.compile(r'\b40[13]\b') matches a bare 401/403 token that is not necessarily an HTTP status, and it is tested before the transport markers (line 201), so a transport failure whose text carries a bounded 401/403 is misclassified as a decisive credential error. Reproduced: fetch_layer with stderr 'dial tcp 10.0.0.1:403: connect: connection refused' (a valid TCP port) and 'dial tcp 10.0.0.1:443: i/o timeout after 403 ms' both raise LayerRegistryCredentialError where the layer state is in fact unknown. Impact: a mirror on port 401/403 or a transport message carrying such a number fails hard instead of skipping - the same skip-vs-fail inversion this delta set out to fix, on a narrower input. Anchoring the match to a status phrase (e.g. 'status code 40[13]') would close it.
